newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire bans protests for duration of war.
newsitem.headline: Zaire bans protests for duration of war.

text.p: Zaire's government on Friday banned public protests and demonstrations until the end of the war against rebels in the east.
Government spokesman Jean-Claude Biebie told state radio after the weekly cabinet meeting that anyone defying the ban would face the full weight of the law.
"The government declares that no public demonstration, no matter its nature, will be authorised throughout the country during the war," Biebie said.
"Whoever goes against this decision will be considered to be in collusion with the enemy and lay himself open to the full weight of the law."
A strike call by the main opposition on Monday virtually shut down the usually teeming capital of five million people.
The main opposition Sacred Union of the Radical Opposition (USOR) of Etienne Tshisekedi called the strike to demand the removal of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
USOR, which has called for negotiations with the rebels, denounced Kengo's conduct of the war and accused him of stalling on promised elections.
Tshisekedi was expected to address his supporters at his party headquarters in Kinshasa on Saturday, to mark the 15th anniversary of the founding of the party.

"Maybe they will send soldiers to disperse the crowd. But I wonder whether it's necessary to apply for an authorisation in order to celebrate one's own birthday," Mukendi wa Mumba, a Tshisekedi adviser, told Reuters.
Non-political groupings planned weekend masses and meetings in memory of victims of a 1992 march by Christians during which security forces fired on the crowd killing dozens of people.
The marchers were protesting against suspension of a national conference discussing democratic reform.
